question_set: 400 distinct questions (58 supported countries x legal topics), not cycled
baseline: existing production: gemma-4-31B classify + preparation (2 sequential calls) then gpt-oss tool-echo search
accuracy_metric: retrieval fidelity vs baseline ranked document IDs (pseudo-gold); reranker HTTP 401 for all (matches prod)

phase1_application_level.measures: analysis + real hybrid search, end-to-end latency

phase2_serving_level_ngram.measures: gemma-4-31B analysis stage (classify + preparation, 2 sequential calls) at 400 questions, on a dedicated slice, baseline serving vs n-gram (prompt-lookup) speculative decoding
phase2_serving_level_ngram.note: n-gram needs numba/NumPy<=2.2; provided via an isolated numpy injected by PYTHONPATH only for the benchmark process (production venv untouched). gpt-oss stopped for the GPU and restarted after (verified healthy).
phase2_serving_level_ngram.output_identity: 392/400 (98%); the few diffs are serving batching nondeterminism, not spec loss (n-gram is provably lossless for greedy)
phase2_serving_level_ngram.verdict: accuracy-preserving serving acceleration; stacks on top of any analysis method (it just speeds the gemma decode of the structured calls)

conclusion: Against the existing baseline (3.73 s, Recall 1.0), the only accuracy-preserving application-level speedups are typed_dispatch (1.18x, Recall 0.994) and parallel analysis (1.28x, Recall 0.995); merge trades a little (1.39x, 0.944) and all aggressive model-substitution methods (fast/compact/cascade) reach ~3.7x but Recall collapses to 0.28-0.38. The accuracy-preserving BIG lever is serving-level: n-gram speculative decoding cuts the gemma analysis stage 47% (2.89->1.53 s) losslessly and stacks with the app-level methods. Recommended accuracy-preserving stack: parallel analysis + typed dispatch + n-gram-served orchestrator.
